devices.name: EverFlo
devices.notes: Philips publishes one average figure (350 W, 120 V model) for all flows, so turning the flow down saves little. Keep backup oxygen cylinders: a 1 kWh battery runs this for under 3 hours.

sources.title: EverFlo brochure, 'EverFlo product specifications' (Average power consumption)

devices.name: Perfecto2 (IRC5PO2 / IRC5P)
devices.notes: Invacare rates 280 W at 3 L/min (120 V model). The Perfecto2 V variant is listed by sellers at about 325 W, which was not confirmed in an Invacare document.

sources.title: Invacare Perfecto2 Oxygen Concentrator User Manual (1143482-H), 10.1 Specifications - Power Consumption

devices.name: 5 Liter (525 series)
devices.notes: US 120 V model: 310 W average, 275 W at 1.2 L/min and below (Turn-Down Technology lowers draw at low flow). 230 V/50 Hz models are rated about 290 W at 2 L/min and 312 W at 5 L/min.

sources.title: DeVilbiss 5 Liter Oxygen Concentrator (525DS) product page, Specifications - Power Consumption
Drive DeVilbiss Compact 525 5 Litre spec sheet, Technical specifications - Power consumption

devices.name: AirSep VisionAire 5
devices.notes: CAIRE lists a single 290 W figure (115 V/60 Hz and 230 V models), so lowering the flow does not save much power.

sources.title: VisionAire 5 User Manual (MN238), Specifications - Power Consumption / Electrical Requirements

devices.name: At Home (GS-100)
devices.notes: Inogen states 100 W at flow setting 2; 275 W is the rated maximum and is used here for 5 L/min as a safe upper bound. Draw rises with the flow setting.

sources.title: Inogen At Home product page, 'Power Settings' (100W on Flow Setting 2)
Inogen At Home User Manual, 9. Specifications, Model GS-100 (AC Power 275 W Max)

devices.name: 10 Liter (1025 series)
devices.notes: High-flow concentrators draw about twice as much as 5 L/min units; a 1.2-1.5 kWh power station runs this for under 2 hours. Plan on oxygen cylinders for long outages.

sources.title: DeVilbiss 10 Liter Oxygen Concentrator (1025DS) product page, Specifications - Power Input 639W (avg), 120VAC 60Hz

devices.name: Other stationary oxygen concentrator (5 L/min)
devices.notes: For models not listed. Most 5 L/min stationary units draw 275 to 350 W at any flow; newer low-power designs draw far less. Check the label or manual for yours.

sources.title: Typical range of the manufacturer figures in this catalog (EverFlo, Perfecto2, DeVilbiss 525, VisionAire 5)

devices.name: One G5

internalBattery.note: single battery at setting 2 (Inogen); up to 6.25-6.5 h at setting 1; double battery up to 10.3 h at setting 2

devices.notes: Inogen does not publish running watts; these are estimated from its battery run times assuming a ~98 Wh single battery plus ~10% for the AC adapter. Draw is higher while the battery is charging, so run on the battery first and recharge when power is available.

sources.title: Inogen One G5 User Manual, 8. Specifications (power inputs, battery duration)
Inogen One G5 Spec Sheet (battery duration on flow setting 1)
How Many Hours Do Portable Oxygen Concentrators Last? (G5 battery duration on flow setting 2)

devices.name: SimplyGo

internalBattery.note: one battery, pulse setting 2 at 20 breaths/min; 1.6 h at continuous 1 L/min, 0.9 h at continuous 2 L/min

devices.notes: Philips lists 120 W while running and 150 W while also charging the battery; the pulse and 1 L/min figures are estimates scaled from Philips battery run times. Pulse mode uses far less power than continuous flow.

sources.title: SimplyGo specifications sheet (PN 1098670), Product specifications - Power consumption; Battery autonomy
SimplyGo User Manual, battery duration table and AC Power Module specifications

devices.name: SimplyGo Mini

internalBattery.note: standard battery at pulse setting 2, 20 breaths/min; up to 9 h with the extended battery

devices.notes: Running watts are derived from Philips figures (97.9 Wh standard battery lasts up to 4.5 h at setting 2) plus about 10% for the AC adapter. Draw can reach 120 W while it also charges its battery.

sources.title: SimplyGo Mini specification sheet, AC power (Power consumption 120 W while charging) and Battery (97.9 Wh; typical duration)

devices.name: FreeStyle Comfort

internalBattery.note: single 8-cell battery at setting 2; double 16-cell battery up to 8 h; up to 8 h / 16 h at setting 1

devices.notes: Watts are estimated from CAIRE's battery-duration table assuming a 14.4 V x 6.7 Ah (about 96 Wh) pack plus ~10% adapter loss; CAIRE gives the mAh but not the pack voltage. Draw is higher while the battery charges.

sources.title: FreeStyle Comfort User Manual (MN250), Specifications (AC/DC power, battery capacity 6700 mAh) and battery duration table

devices.name: AirSense 10 AutoSet
devices.notes: ResMed measured about 7 W for the machine alone versus 34 W with humidifier and heated tube (AutoSet 8-15 cm H2O). Turning both off during an outage makes a battery last about 5 times longer.

sources.title: Power consumption of Air10 devices (ResMed 1018673/1, 2015-03), AirSense 10 AutoSet rows, 'Power Consumed (Watt Hour)'

devices.name: AirSense 10 on ResMed 12 V DC/DC converter

settings.label: Humidifier off, SlimLine tube, 10 cm H2O
Heated tube + humidifier Auto, 10 cm H2O

devices.notes: From ResMed's 12 V current-draw tables (0.93 A to 4.92 A at 10 cm H2O; higher pressures draw more). Running straight from 12 V through the ResMed converter avoids inverter losses; ResMed's battery sizes add a 50% safety margin.

sources.title: ResMed Battery guide (198103/4 2015-08), 'Air10 series' converter tables - current draw at 12 V DC

devices.name: AirSense 11
devices.notes: ResMed lists 56.1 W typical and 73.2 W peak for the AirSense 11 with its 65 W supply; real use is probably lower. The two lower settings are estimates based on ResMed's AirSense 10 measurements. Turn off the humidifier and heated tube to stretch a battery.

sources.title: AirSense 11 User Guide (UK/EU), Technical specifications - 65W power supply unit (typical and peak power consumption)

devices.name: DreamStation 2 (Auto CPAP / CPAP Advanced)
devices.notes: Philips publishes only the input rating (100-240 V, 2.0-1.0 A) and says an 80 W power supply is required for humidification; on a battery pack humidification is switched off. Watts are typical CPAP estimates, not Philips figures.

sources.title: DreamStation 2 CPAP Advanced user manual, Technical specifications - Electrical; 'Check Power' and battery notifications

devices.name: Other CPAP machine
devices.notes: For models not listed. The heated humidifier and tube use most of the power; turning them off during an outage can make a battery last several times longer.

sources.title: Typical range of the ResMed and Philips figures in this catalog

devices.name: AirCurve 10 VAuto
devices.notes: ResMed test: VAuto, PS 6, max IPAP 25, min EPAP 8 cm H2O. The AirCurve 10 S measured 10 / 24 / 43 W for the same three setups; the heated tube and humidifier are most of the load.

sources.title: Power consumption of Air10 devices (ResMed 1018673/1, 2015-03), AirCurve 10 VAuto and AirCurve 10 S rows

devices.name: Trilogy Evo

internalBattery.note: internal + detachable battery, 7.5 h each (Philips nominal per IEC 80601-2-72: AC-VC, active flow circuit, PEEP 3 cm H2O, Vt 800 mL)

devices.notes: Philips publishes battery run time but not average watts; the watts are estimates. Recharging both batteries after an outage adds a large extra load (detachable 0-80% in 2.5 h). A charged spare detachable battery is hot-swappable.

sources.title: Trilogy Evo Accessory guide, 'Trilogy Evo detachable battery (1127889)'
Trilogy EV300 specification sheet (same platform), Electrical - AC/DC input, internal and detachable batteries

devices.name: Astral 100 / 150

internalBattery.note: new 95 Wh internal battery under typical conditions (ACV, Vt 800 mL, PEEP 5, rate 20); more than 4 h worst case

devices.notes: Derived from ResMed figures (95 Wh battery lasts 8 h typical, >4 h worst case) plus ~15% for the power supply. ResMed says the internal battery is not a primary power source; expect up to 90 W (120 W peak) while it recharges after an outage.

sources.title: Astral 100/150 User Guide (APAC), Technical specifications - Power supply, Internal Battery; 'Using the internal battery'

devices.name: Full-electric home care bed
devices.notes: Typical for home care bed motors; draw is brief and only while a motor runs. Lower the bed to a safe height before a forecast outage; some beds have a manual crank or battery backup.

sources.title: Typical value; check the label or manual for your device

devices.name: Alternating-pressure mattress pump
devices.notes: Typical small alternating-pressure pumps draw 5-20 W; check the pump label. Some air cells hold air for hours without power (Drive says up to 24 h for its Med-Aire Plus), but pressure relief stops, so reposition the person regularly.

sources.title: Med-Aire Plus 8" Alternating Pressure and Low Air Loss Mattress System (14029) spec sheet - power outage protection

devices.name: Low-air-loss mattress pump
devices.notes: Typical range 20-120 W because these pumps move more air than alternating-pressure pumps. If the label lists only amps, volts x amps gives an upper bound.

sources.title: Typical value; check the label or manual for your device

devices.name: Patient lift battery charger
devices.notes: Typical for lift chargers; a full lift battery usually covers many transfers. Charge it fully before a forecast outage.

sources.title: Typical value; check the label or manual for your device

devices.name: Home suction machine
devices.notes: Typical values (portable units such as the Vacu-Aide QSU are listed by sellers at 33 W max). Use is brief but critical; many portable units have an internal battery, so keep it charged.

sources.title: Typical value; check the label or manual for your device

devices.name: Nebulizer compressor
devices.notes: Typical piston compressors draw 40-100 W only during treatments (duty cycle assumes 4 x 15 min a day). Battery mesh nebulizers use only a few watts.

sources.title: Typical value; check the label or manual for your device

devices.name: Kangaroo Joey enteral feeding pump

internalBattery.note: new, fully charged battery at 125 mL/h, as listed by distributors; not confirmed in a Cardinal Health document

devices.notes: Typical for small feeding pumps; most runs come from the internal battery. Keep it plugged in until the outage and recharge it first when power returns.

sources.title: Typical value; check the label or manual for your device

devices.name: Home infusion pump
devices.notes: Typical; most home infusion pumps run on internal or AA batteries and draw a few watts when charging. Keep spare batteries as your provider advises.

sources.title: Typical value; check the label or manual for your device

devices.name: HomeChoice Claria APD cycler
devices.notes: Rough estimate (the dialysate warmer dominates); check the rating label on your cycler. Ask your PD nurse about manual exchanges for long outages.

sources.title: Typical value; check the label or manual for your device

devices.name: System One
devices.notes: Rough estimate (fluid warmer plus pumps); check the rating label. A full session may need 1 kWh or more, so contact your dialysis center about outage plans.

sources.title: Typical value; check the label or manual for your device

devices.name: Power wheelchair charger (24 V)

settings.label: Average over a full overnight charge

devices.notes: Typical for 24 V, 8-10 A chargers: draw is highest at the start and tapers off. Top up whenever power is available rather than waiting for empty.

sources.title: Typical value; check the label or manual for your device

devices.name: Mobility scooter charger
devices.notes: Typical for 24 V, 3-5 A scooter chargers. Charge fully before a forecast outage.

sources.title: Typical value; check the label or manual for your device

devices.name: Bedside pulse oximetry monitor
devices.notes: Typical; many bedside monitors have an internal battery good for several hours. A fingertip oximeter on AAA batteries is a useful backup.

sources.title: Typical value; check the label or manual for your device

devices.name: Infant apnea monitor
devices.notes: Typical; most apnea monitors have a rechargeable battery. Check its run time in your monitor's manual and keep it charged.

sources.title: Typical value; check the label or manual for your device

devices.name: Full-size refrigerator
devices.notes: Typical: averages about 50-70 W over a day for a newer model; older units use more, and start-up surge needs inverter headroom. Keep the door shut: a closed fridge stays cold about 4 hours unpowered.

sources.title: Typical value; check the label or manual for your device

devices.name: Mini fridge (compact)
devices.notes: Typical for compact compressor fridges (about 25-30 W averaged over a day). Useful for keeping insulin and other medicines cold.

sources.title: Typical value; check the label or manual for your device

devices.name: 12 V medication cooler
devices.notes: Typical for small 12 V compressor coolers (10-50 W while running). Thermoelectric (Peltier) coolers run almost continuously and use more overall; check storage temperatures with your pharmacist.

sources.title: Typical value; check the label or manual for your device

devices.name: Phone charger
devices.notes: Typical. Charge from a power station's USB ports to skip inverter losses.

sources.title: Typical value; check the label or manual for your device

devices.name: Wi-Fi router + modem
devices.notes: Typical combined draw. Many routers and modems use 12 V adapters, so a DC cable from a power station avoids inverter losses; internet may still be down if the provider loses power.

sources.title: Typical value; check the label or manual for your device

devices.name: LED bulb
devices.notes: Typical. Battery lanterns and headlamps save the power station for medical equipment.

sources.title: Typical value; check the label or manual for your device

devices.name: Laptop
devices.notes: Typical. A USB-C laptop charged from a power station's USB-C port wastes less power than the AC adapter.

sources.title: Typical value; check the label or manual for your device

devices.name: Box fan (20 in)
devices.notes: Typical. A small USB or 12 V fan uses 3-10 W and may be enough near a bed.

sources.title: Typical value; check the label or manual for your device

devices.name: Room humidifier
devices.notes: Typical. Warm-mist (boiling) humidifiers use about 10 times more than ultrasonic models; avoid them on battery power.

sources.title: Typical value; check the label or manual for your device

devices.name: Electric blanket / heated throw
devices.notes: Typical. Keeps a person warm for a small fraction of a space heater's power.

sources.title: Typical value; check the label or manual for your device

devices.name: Electric space heater
devices.notes: 1500 W is the usual maximum for a US plug-in heater; it overloads many power stations and empties a 1 kWh battery in well under an hour. Use blankets or an electric blanket and warm one small room instead.

sources.title: Typical value; check the label or manual for your device

devices.name: Window air conditioner
devices.notes: Typical; the compressor start-up surge can trip smaller power stations (inverter-type units surge less). For heat-sensitive people, cool one small room and use fans.

sources.title: Typical value; check the label or manual for your device
